decisions.title: A very brief possession
decisions.situation: A soap bubble floats past your nose. You reach for it. Your new favourite thing has already resigned.

result.title: Plenty of vacancies
result.body: There are more bubbles. You spend several happy minutes failing to keep any of them.

journal.text: I chased soap bubbles and caught absolutely nothing.

decisions.title: A principled disagreement
decisions.situation: Ruby says shoes are necessary for going outside. You were not consulted during the drafting of this policy.

result.title: Terms accepted
result.body: Both shoes make it onto the correct feet. A surprisingly productive morning.

journal.text: I let Ruby help with my shoes.

decisions.title: Something in your sock
decisions.situation: You hide an ice cube in your sock. Ruby asks why your foot is leaking. You had not planned for questions.

choices.label: Ask to put your sock in the freezer

result.title: One wet sock
result.body: You turn the sock out over a bowl. A tiny cube slides out. Ruby supplies a dry sock; you inspect the bowl for the rest of your treasure.

journal.text: I showed Ruby the ice cube I had hidden in my sock.

decisions.title: The two-headed jacket
decisions.situation: You manage to zip two jackets together. They are now one enormous jacket with four sleeves. This may be your greatest invention.

choices.label: Investigate whether a third one would fit
Leave your invention on the floor

result.title: Back to two jackets
result.body: You work out which zip goes where. Both jackets survive the experiment.

journal.text: I worked out how to separate two jackets I had zipped together.

decisions.title: Forty-two. Definitely forty-two.
decisions.situation: Harper starts a question and your hand shoots up. You have an excellent answer. You are still waiting to hear what the question is.

choices.label: Let someone else risk it first

result.title: A useful last-minute adjustment
result.body: The question is about the number of sides on a triangle. You quietly retire forty-two and give the correct answer.

journal.text: I waited to hear a whole classroom question before answering.

decisions.title: Birthday invitation
decisions.situation: Riley invites you to a birthday party at an arcade. The invitation has more glitter than useful information.

result.title: Adults need an address
result.body: Ruby checks the time and supervision. Their answer and any plan are recorded below. Nothing is paid just for asking.

journal.text: I asked Ruby for permission to go to Riley’s arcade birthday.

decisions.title: Party day
decisions.situation: Riley’s arcade birthday is here. Ruby agreed to take you. The quoted outing costs $29.00, paid by Ruby only if you go.

result.title: High score, low dignity
result.body: You and Riley take turns at the machines. Ruby pays the quoted outing cost. Nobody wins enough tickets to retire.

journal.text: I went to Riley’s arcade birthday with Ruby.

decisions.title: A disappointing lunch
decisions.situation: Riley opens a lunchbox with nothing in it. They look embarrassed. Harper is nearby.

result.title: Lunch gets sorted
result.body: Harper helps without making an announcement. Riley looks relieved.

journal.text: I quietly got Harper’s help when Riley had no lunch.

decisions.title: Indoor architecture
decisions.situation: Rain cancels your afternoon plans. Two chairs and a blanket suggest a career in questionable structural engineering.

result.title: Approved for immediate occupancy
result.body: It collapses twice. The third version has a reading corner.

journal.text: I built a blanket fort that almost met building regulations.

decisions.title: Fastest toy car alive
decisions.situation: You invented the numbers for a marked science report. Your toy car apparently reached 90,000 kilometres an hour. Isla asks to see the original measurements.

choices.label: Admit it and take the report back
Invent a second sheet of measurements

result.title: The car has been recalled
result.body: Isla lets you submit a properly measured replacement with a reduced mark. The real car rolls under a cupboard. You record that too.

journal.text: I admitted inventing science data and replaced my report with real measurements.

decisions.title: Your parent knows this level
decisions.situation: You promise Ruby one last round. They sit down, watch your first attempt and say, “I used to beat this blindfolded.” This is an outrageous development.

choices.label: Agree on one round each, then stop

result.title: Dignity preserved
result.body: You keep your promise and turn it off. Ruby seems more pleased about that than any old high score.

journal.text: I stopped a game when I had promised Ruby I would.

decisions.title: You are in verse two
decisions.situation: Riley asks you to help rehearse a song about everyone who has annoyed them. Your name appears in verse two. The rhyme is frankly weak.

choices.label: Suggest a better rhyme for your insult
Ask why you made the track list

result.title: An unwilling co-writer
result.body: You improve the line and rehearse the chorus. Riley laughs, then admits that your original offence was borrowing a pencil.

journal.text: I helped Riley rehearse a song that included an insult about me.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: recurring wheezing and shortness of breath. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs A$70.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: One star. Still hungry.
decisions.situation: Riley drafts a fake restaurant review of the school canteen. It includes the phrase “structural pasta”.

result.title: Less funny, more useful
result.body: You keep the specific complaints and remove the insults. Isla helps pass it on.

journal.text: I helped Riley turn a canteen rant into useful feedback.

decisions.title: Any difficult questions?
decisions.situation: At a free talk, a speaker claims nobody has ever disproved their theory. The theory is that pigeons remember your face and discuss you at night.

choices.label: Ask how they interviewed the pigeons
Let another questioner take this one
Announce that the pigeons work for you

result.title: The method needs work
result.body: They admit they inferred the conversations. You learn the difference between a suspicious bird and actual evidence.

journal.text: I questioned the evidence behind a speaker’s theory about pigeons.

decisions.title: The sofa is judging you
decisions.situation: Autoplay follows your programme with a competitive fitness class. A man who appears to have been assembled entirely from elbows challenges you to beat your personal best.

choices.label: Switch to the beginner version and try it
Keep up with him at full speed

result.title: An achievable number of elbows
result.body: You complete the gentler routine. The instructor says anyone can do it, then folds himself into a shape you decline to investigate.

journal.text: I followed a beginner workout after a fitness video appeared on autoplay.

decisions.title: Not the tabletop version
decisions.situation: At a craft workshop, you pull the tab on a kit labelled “decorative boat”. A full-size inflatable canoe starts filling the room. The tiny instruction sheet says to inflate outdoors.

choices.label: Deflate it before it reaches the doorway
Climb in and ask for paddles
Insist the picture on the box was misleading

result.title: A long public fart
result.body: You open the valve. The canoe collapses over eight uninterrupted seconds of rude noise. The instructor waits until everyone has stopped laughing to explain the warning.

journal.text: I deflated a full-size canoe during a crowded craft workshop.
